b0d4564j3t.name: TWOMEOW 4 Cup Electric Food Chopper and Meat Grinder
b0d4564j3t.bestFor: Chopping vegetables, meat and baby food in one bowl
b0d4564j3t.description:
The TWOMEOW is a 4 cup electric food chopper with four blades that mince ingredients at the same time. It has two control buttons, one for soft foods such as fruit and vegetables and another for harder items. The bowls are listed as BPA free and food grade, and it can puree and grind as well as chop.

Compared with the BLACK+DECKER 3 cup, it holds a cup more and has a meat grinder role. Against the Ninja Express Chop and its 16 ounce bowl, it has a much larger working size. Against the 1.5 cup Proctor Silex, it suits bigger batches for a family dinner.

Older cooks will like the simple two button layout, which removes the need to pick speeds. Keep fingers away from blades when emptying, and let hot food cool before blending. Wash the bowl by hand or on the top rack, and dry the lid seal to prevent odors. Because the same TWOMEOW also appears in the mini food processor guide, treat the two listings as one product when comparing sellers. Older cooks should keep the cord short and the bowl on a nonslip mat, and let the blades stop fully before opening the lid. Clean the seal after chopping onions or garlic.
pros: Two button controls are easy to learn
Large 4 cup bowl handles family batches
cons: Not a true full size food processor

b01m7srvc3.name: BLACK+DECKER 3 Cup One Touch Food Chopper
b01m7srvc3.description:
The BLACK+DECKER 3 cup chopper uses a one touch button with an improved chopping assembly and lid. Level stainless steel blades are meant to stay sharp, and the listing says you can add oil while mixing for hummus or vinaigrette without making a mess. The 3 cup bowl is a good size for a small household.

Against the TWOMEOW 4 cup, it is a cup smaller but simpler. Against the Ninja Express Chop, it has a larger bowl and a plainer motor. It is the small spaces pick because it stores easily in a cabinet.

Older cooks get a one hand press that is easy on sore thumbs. Cut vegetables into rough chunks first, pulse in short bursts, and unplug the unit before removing the blade. Rinse the lid and bowl promptly so garlic and onion smells do not linger. Grip the bowl firmly when twisting the lid, and keep a small spatula nearby to scrape down thick mixtures. Because the housing is plastic, avoid soaking it, and wipe the motor base with a damp cloth. Replace the unit if the blade assembly wobbles or the lid no longer locks.
pros: One touch button, easy on hands
Add oil through the lid while mixing
3 cup bowl suits a small kitchen
cons: Plastic bowl can scratch over time

b00hl3tbdq.name: Ninja Express Chop 200 Watt Food Chopper, 16 oz
b00hl3tbdq.bestFor: Garlic, herbs and nuts in small batches
b00hl3tbdq.description:
The Ninja Express Chop has a 200 watt power pod and a 16 ounce bowl. The listing says it can mince garlic, onion, zest, spices, herbs, cheese and bacon crumbles, and the ergonomic head is easy to hold. The bowl is smaller than most choppers in this guide.

Compared with the BLACK+DECKER 3 cup and the TWOMEOW 4 cup, it handles much less food at once. It is the premium pick because of its 200 watt motor and the Ninja brand. It suits small jobs rather than large prep.

Older cooks will find the compact size easy to lift and store. Pulse in short bursts, add a splash of liquid for smooth results, and wash the blade carefully. Do not overfill, and let food settle before removing the lid. Because the bowl holds only 16 ounces, process garlic, nuts or herbs in rounds instead of cramming the bowl full. Keep fingers clear when removing the blade, and wipe the underside of the lid, where oil and herb residue gather. Store it on a low shelf, since the power head is easy to drop if lifted from a high cabinet.
pros: Good for garlic, herbs and nuts
cons: Bowl is small for family cooking

b0g7wysx1t.name: Electric Garlic Chopper, 250 ml USB Rechargeable
b0g7wysx1t.bestFor: Garlic, ginger and tiny jobs without a cord
b0g7wysx1t.description:
This is a small 250 milliliter electric garlic chopper that recharges by USB. You press the head down and hold the power button to start it, and release either control to stop. The body comes apart for rinsing, and the listing advises cutting large pieces into smaller chunks first.

It is much smaller than the other choppers here, and it has no cord. Compared with the 3 cup BLACK+DECKER, it handles only a spoonful or two of garlic or herbs. It is the value pick for those who want to avoid hand chopping.

Older cooks with stiff hands may find it helpful for garlic and ginger. Charge it before use, and rinse it right after chopping. Do not run it with hard foods, and check the seal for leaks. Because the data on this listing is limited, look at the product page for the battery size, charging time and bowl material before deciding. Hold the unit steady on the counter while it runs, and never reach into the bowl with fingers. After each use, rinse the parts and dry them, and keep the USB cable in a drawer where it is easy to find.
pros: Light and small enough for a drawer
cons: Needs pre cutting for larger pieces

b007vz0g1u.name: Proctor Silex 1.5 Cup Electric Vegetable Chopper
b007vz0g1u.description:
The Proctor Silex chopper has a 1.5 cup bowl and is described as a small machine for vegetables, purees and chunky onion or peppers. The bowl, lid and removable blades are dishwasher safe. It is small enough to stay on a countertop or tuck into a cabinet.

Against the 3 cup BLACK+DECKER and the 4 cup TWOMEOW, it handles a smaller batch. It is the editor pick for ease of cleaning. Compared with the Ninja, it is plainer but easier to wash.

Older cooks will like dishwasher safe parts. Pulse for chunky results, run longer for puree. Unplug before cleaning and handle blades by the shaft. The small bowl also makes it a sensible second chopper for someone who already owns a larger processor but wants a quick tool for onions, peppers or herbs. It stores easily in a cabinet, the cord is short, and the parts go in the dishwasher. Keep the blade assembly dry and handle it by the center, because the edges are sharp. Wipe the motor base with a damp cloth only, and never submerge it in water.
pros: Dishwasher safe bowl, lid and blades
Pulse control for chunky or smooth results
cons: Not suited to large meal prep

b0d4564j3t.name: TWOMEOW 4 Cup Electric Food Chopper and Grinder
b0d4564j3t.bestFor: Budget shoppers who want a 4 cup capacity
b0d4564j3t.description:
The TWOMEOW is a 4 cup electric chopper with four blades that mince ingredients together. A button marked I is for soft foods and a button marked II is for harder foods. The bowls are BPA free, and the unit can chop, puree and grind.

In this guide it is the value pick. Compared with the 5 cup Cuisinart Chop and Shred, it has no shredding discs. Against the 4 cup Cuisinart with auto reversing blade, it is plainer but also less expensive. It is bigger than the KitchenAid 3.5 cup choppers.

Older cooks like the two button controls. Cut ingredients into chunks first, keep hands clear of blades, and let hot foods cool. Wash the bowl by hand and dry the lid seal. Because the same TWOMEOW also appears in the mini food processor guide, treat the two listings as one product when comparing sellers. Older cooks should keep the cord short and the bowl on a nonslip mat, and let the blades stop fully before opening the lid. Clean the seal after chopping onions or garlic.
pros: 4 cup bowl for family size batches
cons: Less refined than Cuisinart or KitchenAid

b0fpx6f917.name: Cuisinart 5 Cup Chop and Shred Food Processor
b0fpx6f917.bestFor: Cooks who also want to shred cheese and vegetables
b0fpx6f917.description:
The Cuisinart 5 cup Chop and Shred has a work bowl with an ergonomic handle, a reversible disc for fine and medium shredding, and a wide mouth feed tube. A durable universal chopping blade, integrated cord storage and bowl storage are listed. It is the largest unit in this guide.

Compared with the 4 cup Cuisinart, it adds shredding discs. Compared with the KitchenAid 3.5 cup choppers, it handles bigger loads and more tasks. It is the runner up because of its versatility.

Older cooks will like the feed tube, which avoids pre cutting everything. Handle discs by the center, store them in the bowl, and wash parts promptly. The built in cord storage keeps the counter tidy. Compared with the TWOMEOW, it costs more but includes shredding discs, which can save a lot of grating time on cheese and cabbage. Store the discs in the bowl so they do not get lost, and wash the blade with a brush rather than your hand. Always lock the lid fully before starting, and keep the pusher in the feed tube to guide food down.
pros: Cord storage built into the base

b074mqfr55.name: Cuisinart 4 Cup Food Processor with Auto Reversing Blade
b074mqfr55.description:
The Cuisinart small food processor has a 4 cup bowl with a handle, touchpad controls for chop or grind, and an auto reversing SmartPower blade. An exclusive Bladelock system is listed, and a spatula and recipe book are included. Every removable part of the unit is dishwasher safe for easy cleaning.

Compared with the 5 cup Cuisinart, it has no shredding discs. Against the TWOMEOW, it is a more refined design with touchpad control. It is the small spaces pick for its tidy size.

Older cooks will like that the touchpad needs little pressure. Make sure the lid is locked before starting. Use the spatula to scrape the bowl, and place parts on the top rack. Because the SmartPower blade reverses automatically, it can chop and grind without constant stopping, but you should still pulse for delicate herbs. Keep the manual and recipe book together with the bowl. Check the Bladelock fit after cleaning, and store the unit with the cord wrapped loosely to avoid fraying near the plug. Run it only with the lid locked, and keep the bowl on a stable surface away from the counter edge.

b01lxvzi7f.name: KitchenAid 3.5 Cup Food Chopper KFC3516WH
b01lxvzi7f.description:
The KitchenAid KFC3516WH is a 3.5 cup chopper with a locking blade, handle and pour spout. It offers two speeds plus pulse for coarse to fine results, from chunky pico de gallo to purees. A simple cord wrap and a countertop friendly footprint are listed.

This white model is the same machine as the Ice Blue KFC3516IC in this guide, so choose by color. Compared with the Cuisinart 4 cup, it has two speeds but a smaller bowl. It is the editor pick for ease of use.

Older cooks will like the pour spout, which reduces spills. Add liquids for sauces and dressings, and pulse for texture. Wash the bowl and blade after each use, and wrap the cord neatly. Because the Ice Blue model is the same design, pick the color that matches your kitchen and compare seller terms. Use the two speeds for different textures, with the lower speed for pico de gallo and the higher for smooth sauces. Do not fill past the liquid line when making dressings, and rinse the blade promptly after use.
cons: Smaller bowl than the 4 and 5 cup models
Same unit as the Ice Blue listing

b01lz6qn28.name: KitchenAid 3.5 Cup Food Chopper KFC3516IC, Ice Blue
b01lz6qn28.bestFor: Cooks who want the same chopper in a color
b01lz6qn28.description:
The KitchenAid KFC3516IC is the Ice Blue version of the 3.5 cup chopper. It has a locking blade, a handle, a pour spout, two speeds and pulse. The cord wraps neatly into the base.

The listing matches the white KFC3516WH exactly, so color and price are the only differences. It is labeled premium because of its color option. Against the Cuisinart 4 cup, it is smaller but simpler.

Older cooks will find the pour spout and handle useful. Pulse in short bursts, and avoid overfilling. Clean the blade carefully and let parts dry fully. Compared with the 5 cup Cuisinart, it lacks shredding discs, so it is the simpler choice for chopping and pureeing. Add liquid through the opening for sauces, and wipe the pour spout after each use. Store it with the cord wrapped, and replace the blade if it becomes dull. A small spatula is useful for scraping thick mixtures from the bowl. Because its color is the main difference from the white model, check that the finish does not stain from tomato or turmeric, and wash promptly after chopping spices.
cons: Same machine as the white listing

b0clvbqs15.name: EUHOMY Countertop Dishwasher, 6 Programs, 40 dB
b0clvbqs15.description:
The EUHOMY countertop dishwasher measures about 16.8 by 16.7 inches and offers six programs, including Normal, Fast, Glass and Baby. It runs at 40 dB, has 360 degree spray coverage, and uses a built in 5 liter tank or a faucet connection. A heated drying function is also listed on the product page.

In this guide it is the best overall choice because it needs no installation. Compared with the NOVETE and HAVA, it is similar in size, but with a drying feature highlighted. Against the BLACK+DECKER 8 place setting model, it is smaller.

Older owners should note that you fill the tank by hand if there is no faucet nearby. Load plates upright, rinse off large food, and use dishwasher detergent. Empty the tank after each use so stale water does not sit inside. A 5 liter tank is about the size of a small bucket, so plan where to fill it and drain it. Rinse large scraps from plates first, because a small pump handles less debris than a full size machine. Leave the door ajar between uses to let the interior dry, and clean the filter weekly. Allow clearance on all sides for steam.
pros: Built in 5 liter tank means no plumbing
Six programs including Glass and Baby

b0cvx5gby5.name: EUHOMY Countertop Dishwasher, 6 Programs, No Install
b0cvx5gby5.bestFor: Budget buyers needing a quiet countertop unit
b0cvx5gby5.description:
This EUHOMY model also offers six programs and runs at 40 dB, with no installation, tank or faucet needed according to the listing. It dries and keeps dishes fresh for up to 73 hours after washing. The listing says it fits 30 plus pieces.

It looks like a sibling of the top EUHOMY, so check the product page for the exact differences. Compared with the HAVA, it has a stronger quiet focus. It earns the value pick label in this guide.

Older owners will like the low noise. Load carefully, run a hot cycle, and wipe the door gasket. Empty it fully if you leave for a week. Because it looks like a sibling of the top EUHOMY, confirm the capacity and the water source details before ordering. Place it on a firm counter near an outlet, away from the edge. Wipe the door seal after each wash and run an empty hot cycle with a cleaner occasionally. The fresh keeping feature only helps if the door stays closed, so open it only when you are ready to unload.
cons: Small compared with a full dishwasher

b089yd3z91.name: NOVETE Portable Countertop Dishwasher
b089yd3z91.description:
The NOVETE measures about 16.9 by 16.8 by 18.1 inches and holds four full place settings. It supports two water supply modes, including a faucet mode, and offers Normal, Speed, Soft, Baby Care, Heavy and Fruit programs plus a dry mode. A storage rack and cutlery basket are included.

Compared with the HAVA, it has the same dimensions, so they may be rebrands. Against the EUHOMY, it has a stated four place capacity. It earns the compact pick label in this guide.

Older owners can use the faucet mode to avoid refilling. Load the racks carefully, and clean the filter after every few cycles. Four place settings suits one or two people, but a family will need two runs. Keep tall mugs and bowls on the upper rack so spray reaches them, and check the filter often. Let the machine cool before opening the door, as the steam can burn. Choose the faucet mode if it fits your sink, since that avoids carrying water. Dry the interior and leave the door slightly open so mildew does not form inside the sealed tub.
cons: Four place setting capacity is small

b0915x4bbp.name: HAVA R01 Countertop Dishwasher, 6 Programs
b0915x4bbp.bestFor: Single people and couples with small loads
b0915x4bbp.description:
The HAVA countertop dishwasher measures 16.9 by 16.8 by 18.1 inches and uses only about 5 liters of water per cycle. It supports two water supply modes and offers Normal, Speed, Soft, Heavy or Baby Care, Fruit and Dry programs. The maker says each unit goes through quality tests.

It shares its size with the NOVETE, so it is likely a close sibling. Against the BLACK+DECKER, it is lighter and cheaper but smaller. It also earns a compact pick label in this guide.

Older owners should check the hose before the first cycle. Use the faucet mode whenever possible to avoid refilling by hand. At roughly 5 liters of water per cycle, it uses far less water than a hand wash in a running sink, which is a reasonable argument for a small kitchen. Compare it with the NOVETE for price and return terms. Keep detergent tablets in a dry place, and run the Dry program only when you need fully dry plates. Rinse and empty the tank after every use. Always dry the door gasket after the last cycle of the day.
pros: Uses about 5 liters of water per cycle

b08nmvx6xl.name: BLACK+DECKER 18 Inch Portable Dishwasher BPD8B
b08nmvx6xl.description:
The BLACK+DECKER BPD8B is an 18 inch portable dishwasher on wheels with an 8 place setting capacity and an adjustable upper rack. It is Energy Star rated and uses a Quick Connect assembly to attach to a faucet. It can roll to the sink and store away.

Compared with the EUHOMY and HAVA countertop models, it holds about twice as many dishes. It is the premium pick because of capacity and brand. It is a rolling portable unit rather than a countertop box.

Older owners should plan for rolling it to the faucet and for storing it. Connect the hose, load the racks carefully, and check for drips. Eight place settings is enough for a couple with leftovers, and the Energy Star rating suggests it will use less power and water than older portable models. Measure the path from storage to the sink to be sure it rolls smoothly over thresholds. Leave the door open when not in use, and keep the faucet adapter clean. Older owners should check the weight of the unit before ordering, because it is heavier than countertop models.
pros: Rolls on wheels to the sink
